'''Henning Sirringhaus''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is [[Hitachi]] Professor of [[Semiconductor device|Electron Device]] [[Physics]], Head of the Microelectronics Group and a member of the Optoelectronics Group at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]]. He is also a Fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="cam">{{Cite web | url=http://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/directory/sirringhaush | title=Professor Henning Sirringhaus — Department of Physics| date=31 July 2013}}</ref><ref name="whoswho">{{Who's Who | title=SIRRINGHAUS, Prof. Henning | id = U255755 | volume = 2014 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Chua | first1 = L. ==Education==
Sirringhaus was educated at [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]] where he was awarded a Bachelor of Science degree and PhD in physics.<ref>{{Cite thesis|first=Henning|last=Sirringhaus|title=Ballistic-electron-emission microscopy on epitaxial CoSi₂ / Si interfaces |publisher=ETH Zurich |year=1995 | doi = 10.3929/ethz-a-001486644|authorlink=Henning Sirringhaus|hdl=20.500.11850/142196|type=Doctoral Thesis}}</ref> From 1995 to 1996 he worked as a [[postdoctoral research]] fellow at [[Princeton University]].<ref name="cam"/>

==Research==

==Awards and honours==
Sirringhaus was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 2009, his nomination reads: {{centred pull quote|Henning Sirringhaus is distinguished for his work on semiconductor device physics and engineering. Early in his career, at the ETH Zurich, he pioneered the technique of [[ballistic electron emission microscopy]]. At Cambridge he has transformed the field of [[organic semiconductor]] [[transistor]]s from curiosity to fully manufacturable technology through both fundamental science and engineering. His insights into the [[polaron]]ic nature of [[Electron configuration|electron state]]s in these materials and the control of [[Interface (chemistry)|interfacial structure]] made possible large increases in field-effect carrier mobility. His work on novel processing methods, including [[Inkjet printing|ink-jet printing]], has made possible new manufacturing methods. A recent highlight is his realisation of a [[Organic field-effect transistor|light-emitting field-effect transistor]].<ref name="royal">{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC%2F2009%2F35%27) |title =Library and Archive Catalogue EC/2009/35: Sirringhaus, Henning |publisher=The Royal Society |archivedate=2014-04-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20140404094300/http://royalsociety.org/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo=='EC/2009/35') |location=London}}</ref>}}
